title: Sakuya configuration
description: sakuya.config.json, at the repository root. The only place Sakuya is configured; every key is optional. Restart after editing.

port.description: Port the API server listens on. The web dev server proxies /api here. Ignored in Docker, which pins 3777.

host.description: Interface to bind, for both the API and the web dev server. 127.0.0.1 = this machine only. 0.0.0.0 = reachable from your network; turn auth on first, since the server exposes your whole library and can open a file manager on this machine. Ignored in Docker, which must bind 0.0.0.0.

dataDir.description: Where the database, thumbnails, uploads and models live. null = autodetect: ~/.sakuya if that folder exists, else apps/server/data. A relative path is relative to this file. Setting it disables the move button in Settings > System. Ignored in Docker, which mounts the data dir at /data.

https.description: Mark the login cookie Secure. Only turn on when serving over HTTPS: browsers silently drop Secure cookies over plain HTTP, which would lock you out.

port.description: Port of the web interface (the Vite dev server). In Docker the web interface is served by nginx; change its published port in docker-compose.yml.

enabled.description: Require a password to use Sakuya.

secret.description: The password. Required when auth is enabled. Changing it signs every session out.

cpus.description: CPU budget in cores; fractions allowed (1.5). Sizes background job concurrency and the ffmpeg / AI tagger / image-processing thread pools, and is enforced as a hard cap on Linux (systemd) and Windows (job object). In Docker, set `cpus` in docker-compose.yml instead; the app detects it. null = no limit.

memory.description: Memory ceiling: "2g", "512m", "1.5g", or a byte count. Enforced as a hard cap on Linux (systemd) and Windows (job object): past it, allocations fail rather than the machine swapping. Not enforceable on macOS. In Docker, set `mem_limit` in docker-compose.yml instead. null = no limit.
